official_measurement_examples.name: Removal and management regimes separated
official_measurement_examples.fact: RPA statutory guidance states the 2024 management regulations cover agricultural hedgerow management, while hedgerow removal remains governed separately by the Hedgerows Regulations 1997.

official_measurement_examples.name: Protected countryside hedgerow scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK removal guidance applies protection tests based on hedgerow length, location and importance, and excludes hedges in or marking the boundary of a private garden from that regime.

official_measurement_examples.name: Removal notice timing
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK states the local planning authority normally has a 42-day period to respond to a hedgerow-removal notice and may issue a retention notice or written removal permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2024 no-cut period
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Management of Hedgerows rules prohibit cutting or trimming covered agricultural hedgerows from 1 March to 31 August inclusive, subject to specified exceptions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Two-metre buffer rule
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2024 rules require reasonable steps to maintain green cover within 2 metres of the centre of a covered hedgerow and restrict cultivation plus fertiliser or pesticide application there, subject to exceptions.

official_measurement_examples.name: RPA enforcement role
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Rural Payments Agency acts as regulator for the 2024 management rules and can use civil sanctions or prosecution according to the statutory framework and enforcement approach.

official_measurement_examples.name: Wildlife law remains separate
official_measurement_examples.fact: RPA guidance makes clear hedgerow-management exemptions are limited to those rules and do not automatically remove separate wildlife-law duties such as nesting-bird protection.

official_measurement_examples.name: Permission separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Hedgerow-removal permission, agricultural management compliance, planning permission and land ownership are separate questions and none should be inferred from another.

core_rules: hedgerow removal permission is not planning permission
planning permission is not automatically hedgerow removal permission
2024 agricultural hedgerow management compliance is not removal permission
1997 removal protection and 2024 management rules must not be merged
a 2 metre agricultural buffer strip is not a universal planning-development setback
the 1 March to 31 August management period is not evidence a hedge can lawfully be removed outside that period
a management exemption is not a blanket wildlife-law exemption
garden-boundary hedges must not be silently treated as covered by the countryside removal regime
protected hedgerow status depends on the statutory criteria rather than hedge appearance alone
an important-hedgerow retention notice is not a land-ownership decision
RPA management enforcement is distinct from local-planning-authority removal decisions
scheme payment eligibility is not planning permission
historic hedgerow records must retain survey date location and legal regime
hedgerow compliance does not reserve development capacity or create access rights
no parcel hedgerow clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official GOV.UK, RPA and legislation.gov.uk sources were checked on 2026-07-26. The 1997 removal regime and 2024 management regime were kept distinct; March-August cutting and two-metre buffer rules were not converted into planning-clearance claims.
